extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'host' is concatenated directly into an OS command string via os.system(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. ';', '|', backticks) to execute arbitrary commands on the server. Example: ?host='127.0.0.1;cat /etc/passwd'

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'endpoint' query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without any URL validation or allowlisting. This enables Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — an attacker can probe internal services, access cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/), or read local files via file:// URLs.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is passed directly as a Jinja2 template string via Template().render(). Jinja2 templates execute Python code, allowing full remote code execution. An attacker can send fragment={{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} or use the environment object to read/write files and execute arbitrary commands.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The entire request JSON body is used as a MongoDB query filter in find_one(query). The variable 'query' equals payload.get('filter', payload) — if the user does not provide a 'filter' key, the whole body becomes the query. An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g. {$ne: null}, $where) to bypass authentication, extract data, or execute server-side JavaScript.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in NoSQL Query (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: The 'name' form parameter is used directly as part of a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) without any traversal guard. An attacker can pass '../' sequences in 'name' to write or overwrite arbitrary files on the filesystem, such as ../../etc/passwd or other critical system files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: User-controlled 'copyline' query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML string and returned as HTMLResponse without any escaping or sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript: ?copyline=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Hardcoded default values for SSN ('111-22-3333') and credit card number ('4111111111111111') are written to disk when the user omits those fields. Additionally, unsanitized user-supplied SSN and credit card data is persisted in plaintext to an arbitrary file path on the server via write_text(). This creates sensitive PII exposure via CWE-359/CWE-200.

cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data

extra.message: The 'Origin' HTTP header is reflected directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header with credentials ('true'). An attacker-controlled Origin can bypass same-origin policy when cookies or other credentials are present. This should only allow known, explicitly configured origins rather than reflecting arbitrary input.

User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without validation of the redirect target. An attacker can craft a link like /ops/after/ticket-lane-148?lane=https://evil.com/phish that appears to originate from this trusted domain.

SSL/TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled via ssl._create_unverified_context() when making an outbound HTTPS request to a hardcoded target URL. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks on webhook delivery and any other calls using this pattern.

The 'random' module's choice() function uses the Mersenne Twister PRNG which is not cryptographically secure and its output is predictable. This nonce/random code generation endpoint should use 'secrets' / 'secrets.token_urlsafe()' instead to generate unguessable values.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The webhook HMAC signature uses hook.secret_hash (a SHA-256 hash of the actual secret) as the signing key instead of the original plaintext secret. This means an attacker who compromises the stored secret_hash can compute valid HMAC signatures without knowing the actual secret, and cannot be rotated without re-storing secrets.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Debug mode is enabled by default (debug: True). In Python frameworks like FastAPI/Uvicorn, debug mode can expose stack traces, sensitive environment variables, and internal application state to attackers in error responses.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Cookie secure flag defaults to False (cookie_secure: bool = False), meaning session cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. Combined with cookie_samesite='lax', this creates a risk of CSRF and credential theft on public or compromised networks.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Set-Cookie' Header Without 'Secure' Attribute
